what: M8 blind holdout (plan section 7.20): 50 fresh agreements, all ten concepts, union stage 1 (v7 rules plus the Haiku picker), schema v2.10 and the post-checks; one Sonnet run against Opus gold adjudicated under v2.10. Pooled with M7 run 2 (v2.9 extraction, v2.10 post-checks and gold).

schema_ambiguous.reason: The only mention is a tax representation (3.08(p)) that no Section 336(e) election will affect post-closing items. The schema says present if the agreement 'mentions' an election, but the concept is an election in this deal, so a rep about past elections is unresolved; gold left absent.

Closing conditions 4.1.3 and 4.1.4 use an undefined lowercase 'material adverse change' described inline; v2.5 rule 10 covers a capitalized term (present) and a lowercase term used only in passing (absent), not an operative undefined MAC condition (same ruling as earlier holdouts). Gold left present.

Both arms code nearly identical carve-outs per definition and differ on which definition is target_side: in this de-SPAC the operating Company issues ADSs and GF becomes its subsidiary, so v2.1 rule 11 points to GF as target while the v2.2 rule 9 de-SPAC treatment points to the Company. Gold also adds political_war_terrorism to the general-conditions clause (f)/(d) contrary to v2.3 rule 11; left as is.

Clause (e) ends its war, disaster and pandemic list with "any other force majeure event"; the schema does not say whether a residual force-majeure catch-all adds other or falls under the listed codes, so both readings are defensible.

Section 10.2(k) says Target 'shall reimburse Parent $25.3 million' on an outside-date termination but never says what is reimbursed. Next to the 10.2(j) refund of the $43.5M Plains fee, it may be a partial refund of that named one-off cost (v2.1 rule 10, not a fee), or it may be a fixed termination payment. The schema does not decide which.

S103 says only that 'the tax consequences of any deemed asset sale under IRC Section 338' are for Buyer's account. A deemed sale needs a 338 election, but no election is named. The schema says present only if an election is mentioned and does not decide whether this indirect reference counts.

Section 6.16 states a shared intent to get asset-acquisition treatment ('whether as a result of an election under section 338(g) ... or otherwise') and says both parties 'shall take reasonable steps to ensure such treatment'. The schema never defines joint against mandatory_joint, and the text names no party that makes the election.

Clause (y) bars either party from terminating until 60 days after a Required Governmental Consent is obtained when only Final Order status is missing; it works like a regulatory-pending later date (v2.5 rule 8) but is drafted as a bar on terminating, which v2.5 rule 8 says is not an extension. The schema does not decide which governs.
